questions.q: Which msdb table records metadata for every backup SQL Server has ever taken, regardless of how it was run?
options: msdb.dbo.backupset
msdb.dbo.sysjobhistory
sys.databases
msdb.dbo.sysjobs
questions.explain: backupset logs every completed backup — full, differential, or log — independent of any Agent job.

questions.q: In msdb.dbo.backupset, what does the type column value 'I' mean?
options: Differential backup
Full (database) backup
Log backup
Index rebuild operation
questions.explain: In backupset, 'D' is full, 'I' is differential, and 'L' is a log backup.

questions.q: A query against backupset shows NULL in the last_full column for a database. What does that mean?
options: That database has never had a full backup taken
The full backup succeeded but the file was deleted afterward
The database is in SIMPLE recovery model
The backupset table simply hasn't been refreshed yet
questions.explain: A NULL means there is no row in backupset for a full backup of that database — it has never been backed up.

questions.q: What does msdb.dbo.backupmediafamily provide that backupset alone does not?
options: The physical file path(s) a given backup was actually written to
The SQL statement text used to run the backup
The recovery model of the database at backup time
The name of the Agent job that triggered the backup
questions.explain: backupmediafamily links a backup set to its physical_device_name — the actual file location.

questions.q: Why might a DBA query backupset directly instead of trusting SQL Server Agent job history alone?
options: A job can report success on a step while a backup silently didn't happen, or fail for an unrelated reason while the backup actually completed
Agent job history is deleted automatically after 24 hours
backupset is faster to query than sysjobhistory
sysjobhistory doesn't exist in msdb
questions.explain: Job history reflects job step outcomes, not necessarily whether a usable backup exists — backupset is the definitive record.
